subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 8: Literacy – Reading brochures and adverts
outcomes: Skim a brochure to find its type and purpose.
Scan a brochure for facts about four holidays.
Spot persuasive words in brochures and adverts.

tf.s: A brochure often tries to get you to buy something or go somewhere.
tf.why: Yes, brochures are written to persuade.

tf.s: You can watch penguins on the safari holiday.
tf.why: Penguins are on the polar holiday in the Antarctic.

tf.s: On the safari holiday you can see oryx in Oman.
tf.why: Correct, the safari adventure shows oryx in Oman.

tf.s: The safari tour groups are small so you can get close to the animals.
tf.why: Well done, small groups get closer to the animals.

tf.s: The climbing holiday is in the Antarctic.
tf.why: You climb up rocks in Spain on the climbing holiday.

tf.s: Sandboarding in Oman is on the extreme sport holiday.
tf.why: Yes, sandboarding is an extreme sport.

tf.s: Persuasive adjectives in adverts are always 100% true.
tf.why: Be careful: persuasive words may not always be true.
Right, stunning scenery is very beautiful.

tf.s: An expert is someone who is new to an activity.
tf.why: An expert knows a lot and has done it for a long time.

tf.s: When you skim, you look quickly at the title, headings and pictures.
tf.why: Good! Skimming gives you the main idea fast.

boxes.q: What type of text is Adams' Adventures?
boxes.why: It is a brochure for adventure holidays.
Penguins are in the Antarctic on the polar holiday.

boxes.q: Which holiday lets you climb rocks in Spain?
boxes.why: Climbing up rocks in Spain is the climbing holiday.

boxes.q: Why do brochures use positive words?
Complete: Walking across ___ green hills is lovely.
boxes.why: Gentle hills are soft and not steep.

boxes.q: Laith has been a diver for many years. He's a real diving ___.
boxes.why: An expert has a lot of skill and experience.
Terrific is a strong positive adjective.

boxes.q: Go sandboarding in Oman: which holiday?
boxes.why: Sandboarding is on the extreme sport holiday.

boxes.q: What do you look at first when you skim?
boxes.why: Skimming means looking quickly at the main parts.

hunt.q: A person with lots of skill

mcq.q: What is the purpose of the Adams' Adventures text?
o: to get you to go on an adventure holiday
to tell a story about a family
mcq.why: A brochure persuades readers to book a holiday.

mcq.q: Which animals can you see on the safari adventure in Oman?
mcq.why: The safari adventure shows oryx in Oman.

mcq.q: Which group of words are all persuasive adjectives?
mcq.why: These are strong positive adjectives that persuade.

mcq.q: 'Watch penguins in the Antarctic.' Which holiday is this?
mcq.why: Penguins live in the Antarctic, so it is the polar holiday.

mcq.q: Choose the best word: Our guides are ___ who know everything about the desert.
mcq.why: Experts know a lot about something.

mcq.q: You want the main idea of a brochure in one minute. What should you do?
o: skim the title, headings and pictures
mcq.why: Skimming gives you the main idea quickly.

mcq.q: Why are the safari tour groups small?
o: so you can get close to the animals
mcq.why: Small groups help visitors get closer to animals.

mcq.q: An advert says 'the perfect holiday'. What should a careful reader think?
o: It may not be completely true; it is trying to persuade.
It must be true because it is printed.
It is a fact from science.
It is a rule you must follow.
mcq.why: Persuasive words try to sell, so read them carefully.

o: Come and enjoy terrific views on a stunning trip!
mcq.why: Strong adjectives like terrific and stunning persuade readers.
